name: Qwen3.8-27B
pitch: A 27-billion-parameter model that reads images too, fast on one DGX Spark.
architecture: 64 layers: 48 recurrent (Gated DeltaNet) and 16 full-attention, with a vision tower. TandemLLM runs it with two small draft models: they guess the next tokens and one pass of the big model checks them all, so a pass can keep several tokens. With greedy decoding the text is the model's own, up to near ties.
license: The model's license is on its Hugging Face page. TandemLLM itself is AGPL-3.0 or commercial.

devices.label: NVIDIA DGX Spark (128 GB unified memory)
devices.note: The GPU and the CPU share this memory. MemTotal reads 121.6 GiB of the 128 GB.

assets.label: Draft models (EXL3 K3)
assets.source: Converted on the reference box (ENG-215) and published in 0xBakeer/TandemLLM-Qwen3.8-27B-EXL3-drafters (exl3-drafters-k3/). Each file holds one drafter's projections; the drafter's BF16 checkpoint (nvfp4-drafters) gives the rest.

assets.label: Draft head (EXL3 K4)
assets.source: Converted on the reference box (ENG-215) and published in 0xBakeer/TandemLLM-Qwen3.8-27B-EXL3-drafters (exl3-draft-head-k4/).

assets.label: Base checkpoint (Qwen3.8-27B-FP8)
assets.source: Public on Hugging Face. Every 27B profile reads its embeddings, norms, the tensors the quantised weights leave and the tokenizer; not mtp.safetensors (the 27B drafts with its own drafters). install.sh downloads it, except with --setup; use-profile.sh downloads it when it is missing (NVFP4; the EXL3 profiles need base-plain, which it serves for).

assets.label: Base tensors for EXL3 (Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 without its FP8 projections)
assets.source: OPS-133: the tensors of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 an EXL3 load reads, fetched by range requests: the embedding, the norms, the GDN gates and convolutions, the vision tower, the config and the tokenizer (3.54 GB of 30.41). Left out: the F8_E4M3 projections with their scales (24.33 GB) and lm_head.weight (2.54 GB), which every EXL3 pack here quantises (tests/test_base_plain.py). A box with base-fp8 uses that instead.

assets.label: Draft models (DFlash2 b8 and b16, BF16)
assets.source: The 0.4.8 release's drafters (DFlash2-b8 and -b16 on Hugging Face, BF16), read from the repository's train/ folder (CKPT8, CKPT16). The NVFP4 profile quantises their projections at load; an EXL3 profile replaces them with the K3 files, named after these folders.

measurements.method: tools/exl3_fastrun.py, one raw-engine server per run, prompts prose / chat / code, 3 reps, temperature 0 (greedy) or 0.7 with top-p 0.95 (sampled), thinking off, 128 or 512 new tokens, 2 runs a mode (6 decodes a cell); long rows: the code task after 32k / 64k tokens of held-out text, one text a cell; lossless: tools/exl3_lossless.py, 12 traces of 256 tokens against the size's own greedy decode. Caches, the conductor and the small models off; 4 slots of 262,144 tokens with the KV pool on. Chat and long rows are one prompt a cell: read them as "smaller is faster", not as an order between neighbours.

rows.note: Older build 0.4.8, not comparable with the rows above. One run with the NVFP4 drafters, greedy 512 prose and chat only (kernel note "2026-10-08 23:35 CEST").

components.label: Draft models
components.what: Two small models guess the next tokens, and the big model checks the guesses in one pass. Most of the speed comes from here.
components.note: The weight profile picks which draft models load. Their memory is the profile's drafters_gib, and their context KV is part of the 104.25 KiB a token below.

components.label: Lookup store
components.what: Remembers what the model read and wrote before and suggests it again when text repeats, like code you edit many times.
components.note: 192 MiB of token ids at most (--suffix-store-mb), in host memory.

components.label: Conductor
components.what: Gives each request the right instructions and helper packages, and watches long sessions so they do not get stuck.
components.note: Off, clients talk to the raw engine and the small models below have nothing to do.

components.label: Narrator
components.what: A small model that writes short status lines while the big model thinks, so you can see what it is doing.
components.note: Qwen3.5-2B, 3.60 GiB in the live memory split. When memory runs short it goes after the shadow reader and loads again later. Off by default since 0.11.3 (SRV-534); turned on, it serves the model, and the lines come with the roles document's narrator mode and a profile's ui.narrator.

components.label: Laya decision models
components.what: Three tiny classifiers that answer the conductor's quick questions, like what kind of request this is, in milliseconds.
components.note: Without them the big model answers those questions itself, which costs a turn each time.

components.label: Shadow reader
components.what: A small model that reads along with each session when the box is idle, so later questions about it are answered fast.
components.note: Qwen3.5-0.8B (1.52 GiB in the live memory split) and up to 4 GiB of session states (QWEN38_SHADOW_GB). The first to unload when memory runs short.

components.label: Vision
components.what: Lets the model read images you send with a message.
components.note: The tower ships inside the base checkpoint. The extra 0.5 GiB is the cache of encoded images (--image-cache-mb 512).

components.label: Conversation cache
components.what: Keeps the conversation the model is in, so the next turn starts where the last one ended instead of reading everything again.
components.note: The resident prefix, 0.43 GiB in the live memory split. At their caps the anchors take 2.5 GiB, the stash 1, the pin 4 and the park 4. Off, every agent turn reads its whole prompt again.

components.label: State store
components.what: Saves the model's state after short chats, so the same start a second time costs nothing.

components.label: Response cache
components.what: Answers an identical greedy request again from memory, without running the model.
components.note: Off on the reference box. Useful for scripts that send the same request many times; never for a benchmark.

components.label: Disk cache
components.what: Keeps the start of long prompts on the SSD, so a long agent session or a returning chat starts in seconds.
components.note: 16 GB by default (the Memory screen sets it), in a folder per weight profile. It never takes the disk under 50 GB free.

components.label: Session spill
components.what: Moves a paused conversation to the SSD instead of dropping it, and brings it back on its next turn.
components.note: Compressed, up to SESSION_SPILL_GB (64 GB), inside the disk cache's folder.

components.label: Other backends
components.what: Lets the dashboard send some model names to other servers or cloud APIs, beside this engine.
components.note: You add the backends later, on the Backends screen.

methods.label: Sampled decoding
methods.what: How a request with a temperature is checked against the draft. det uses the same tree as a greedy request and is the fastest; the answers still follow the model's own sampling.

options.label: mixed: the sampled chain in the tree

methods.label: Thinking effort
methods.what: How long the model may think before it answers, when a client does not say.

methods.label: Default answer length
methods.what: The longest answer, in tokens, when a client does not set max_tokens.

methods.label: Draft temperature
methods.what: How sharp the draft models' guesses are on a sampled request. Lower means fewer wrong guesses.

methods.label: Request time limit
methods.what: Seconds one request may run before the engine stops it.

methods.label: Queue length
methods.what: How many requests may wait for a free slot before new ones are turned away.

methods.label: Queue wait
methods.what: Seconds a request may wait in the queue before it gets an error.

advanced.label: Port
advanced.what: The port the API and the dashboard answer on.

advanced.label: Listen on
advanced.what: The whole network, or only this machine.

advanced.label: Raw engine name
advanced.what: The model name of the raw engine. With the conductor on, clients see TandemLLM and this name is a hidden alias.

advanced.label: Dashboard login
advanced.what: With an admin password set, on makes the dashboard ask for it too.

advanced.label: Admin password
advanced.what: Without one, anyone who reaches the port can change the setup. Generate writes a random one into secrets.env on the box; read it there with cat.
